title: Adoption, completeness and reporting time after the introduction of structured abdominal CT reports: a prospective observational study
abstract: Objective: to describe adoption of a structured template, completeness of key elements for three index questions, reporting time and referrer views in the six months after introduction. Design: prospective observational study with rated free-text reports from the previous six months as context. Results will follow data collection.
introduction: Structured reports are more complete in most studies, but adoption plateaus and overrides are common, and historic comparisons can be unfair to free-text reports.
methods: Each month 25 reports per index question are sampled at random and rated against a fixed checklist; template use is recorded as opened, completed and completed without override. Historic free-text reports are rated with a stated-or-clearly-implied rule fixed in advance. Active reporting time comes from system time stamps and referrer views from a five-item questionnaire at months 3 and 6.
results: Data collection starts on 2027-01-11. The report will give completeness by index question with intervals, monthly run charts of adoption and reporting time, and referrer scores.
discussion: To be written. The comparison with historic reports will be treated as context, not as an effect estimate.
limitations: No concurrent comparison; the checklist was designed with the template.
conclusion: To be written after six months of data.
reportingChecklist: STROBE, with SQUIRE 2.0 items for the description of the change
